Une instance {0}, c'est une machine qui:
A {0} instance is a machine that answers. Inviting someone is giving them the means to talk to it.

Two steps, in this order:

- Open your instance. Settings, Profile, “Open my instance to my colleagues”. While it is closed, it answers only your machine. On opening, it starts encrypting its exchanges and shows the addresses at which it can be reached.
- Invite the person by their email address. They receive a link: one click, and their machine attaches. Without a clickable link, the address and the code from the email can be typed by hand, or pasted together into the first field.

How they reach you depends on where they are:

- Same network. Same Wi-Fi, same office, same cable: nothing to set up, the address is enough. This is the common case.
- Elsewhere. They then need a private link between your two networks: your company VPN, or a private network set up between your machines. {1} detects it on its own and shows the matching address. Do not open a port on your router to get there faster: you would expose your machine to the whole internet, and gain nothing.
- Round the clock. With your machine switched off, your instance no longer answers: it is the one running the models. For a team working continuously, install the instance on a machine that never switches off.

What the invitation code is worth: seven days, a single use, a single email address. The person chooses their own password, which you will never know. You can cancel an invitation as long as it has not been used. When the email goes out, the code is shown only to the invited person, in their mailbox: that is what proves they really read this address.

The administrator can also create an account directly. The password they choose is temporary: at first sign-in, the person chooses their own, and the old one no longer works.

The first attachment will show a certificate warning: your instance signs its own, and no outside authority knows it. You accept once, and the application will then refuse any different certificate.

Une tâche programmée, c'est une consigne:
A scheduled task is an instruction and a rhythm: the instance runs it with your tools (emails, calendar, files), even with the window closed, then keeps its report.

- Where: Tasks, “Scheduled” section, “New scheduled task”. Or in a Chat: “Every Monday at 8 am, summarise my emails from the week”. A card shows it to you before it is created.
- Rhythm: every day, Monday to Friday, every week (a chosen day), every month (a day of the month, or the last one), and the time.
- Done by: the Chat agent, or one of your agents, with its instructions, its model and its knowledge bases.
- Each run leaves a report, which opens in a Chat to reply to it.

Nobody is in front of the screen when it runs: anything that changes something waits for your approval, and without an answer the card expires, except at the “Approve everything” level. A machine switched off at the set time runs the task at the next start, once.
